scope: Additional controlled membrane candidates on unchanged existing exchange edges; no new edge or moved anchor

method.componentDefinition: M.allowed radius mask, siege radius plus sqrt(2)/8-world sweep reserve; four neighbors with edge midpoints
method.centerlineSampling: Segment interior sample spacing <=0.5 source px, both perpendicular normals; original edge centerlines only
method.boneCheck: Minimum distance to every existing ReferenceMap.bones capsule minus capsule radius; must clear siege radius plus sweep reserve. This is coarse existing bone geometry only.
method.selection: One maximum-score candidate per sampled tissue component, prioritizing unchanged navigation-fix deep target component. Full gate traversal has NOT been tested.

limitations: Sampling checks candidate radius masks, not actual Path/Workers motion or gate transitions. Components may include legal gate apertures and must not be mistaken for pure lane-zero reachability.
brain and bladder boundaries are coarse_locator, not fine_visual. Limbs/trunk have no matching zones.

The large siege radius plus sweep reserve is used for component surveys. Smaller cells can differ. Previous target endpoint [517,417] is not siege-clear; do not move or replace frozen targets to claim acceptance.
All vessel walls currently affect same-plane tissue irrespective of per-edge display layer. Some apparent partitions may be depth-model problems; review ownership/layers before creating gates.
0.5 source-pixel grid with midpoint checks cannot certify continuous connectivity or rule out narrower alternate paths.
No original anatomical image, geometry, gate, route, production file or saved-state version was modified.
No match means this restricted finite normal scan found none, not mathematical impossibility.
Candidates still require swept legal gate crossing, reachable lumen anchor, target route, return route, all three cell sizes, and negative sealed-wall tests.
brain and bladder candidate outlines remain coarse. Their outputs must not be called fine-boundary acceptance.
